data.title: Placeholder
data.tagline: A placeholder is the gray example inside an input box showing the expected format; it vanishes the moment you type.
data.learningOutcome: You can separate the placeholder's job from the label's, and know "gray text disappears" is normal while "label disappears" is a bug.
data.description: The gray you@example.com in an email box demonstrates "fill it like this" and steps aside at the first keystroke. It splits the job with the label: the label sits beside the box and stays, while the placeholder only opens the show—once typing starts, only the label tells you what the field is.

learning.assumes: You have typed into web inputs and seen gray example text inside them.
learning.outcome: You can separate the placeholder's job from the label's, and know "gray text disappears" is normal while "label disappears" is a bug.

distinctions.label: Label
distinctions.explanation: Label stays beside the input the whole time; Placeholder is the gray example inside that disappears once you type.

distinctions.label: Input
distinctions.explanation: Input is the control you type into; Placeholder is only the temporary hint shown inside it before typing.

explanation.title: Demonstrating format
explanation.text: The best placeholders show format: a gray 2026-03-12 in a date box or you@example.com in an email box tells the shape at a glance.

explanation.title: Not carrying explanations
explanation.text: The placeholder vanishes once typing starts. If the field's meaning lives only in the placeholder, it is forgotten halfway—that job belongs to the label.

explanation.title: Not a required marker
explanation.text: "Required" needs a star or explicit text by the label; users routinely skip gray example text, so rules cannot live there.

data.boundary: The form-check mantra: if you still know what the field is after typing, the label is doing its job; if the box goes blank, the form was placeholder-only. Overly faint placeholders also read as disabled—ask for readable light gray.

lessonPractice.title: When the user starts typing, which of these disappears?

options.label: The gray example text inside the box
options.feedback: Correct. The placeholder yields the moment typing starts—which is why it cannot replace the label.

options.label: The "Email" label beside the box
options.feedback: The label stays beside the box through typing—that is exactly its job.

options.label: Neither disappears
options.feedback: The placeholder does disappear once typing begins; if it stays, the implementation is off.

data.agentPrompt: Give every input a permanently visible label; use placeholder text only to demonstrate format, like you@example.com in the email box. After filling in, I should still tell what each field is.
